pages.name: welcome
pages.text_excerpt: Welcome to TunaOS Welcome. This assistant will guide you through installing TunaOS onto this computer. You will choose a target disk and a few options. Nothing is written to any disk until you confirm on the last step. Get started

pages.name: disk
pages.text_excerpt: Select a disk Everything on the disk you pick will be erased. Samsung SSD 870 EVO 500GB /dev/sda · 465.8 GiB · SATA Extreme SSD /dev/sdc · 931.5 GiB · USB Cruzer Blade /dev/sdd · 59.6 GiB · USB WD_BLACK SN850X 1000GB /dev/nvme0n1 · 953.9 Gi

pages.name: options
pages.text_excerpt: Options Sensible defaults are already chosen. Change them only if you need to. System Computer name ubuntu Filesystem xfs Encryption Disk encryption No encryption Anyone with the disk can read your files. Back Continue

pages.name: confirm
pages.text_excerpt: Confirm installation The last screen before anything is written. Everything on /dev/sda will be erased. This cannot be undone.  Summary Target disk /dev/sda Filesystem xfs Encryption No encryption Computer name ubuntu Image ghcr.io/tuna-os/

pages.name: done
pages.text_excerpt: TunaOS is installed Remove the installation media and restart the computer. Restart now Close

pages.name: recovery
pages.text_excerpt: TunaOS is installed Remove the installation media and restart the computer. Save your recovery key If your disk fails to unlock automatically, you will need this recovery key to access your data. Save it somewhere safe, like a password mana

notes: Text comes from the strings the harness rendered each page from (the same constants the view reads), not from a widget tree or OCR, so this reports SCREEN PARITY only. It does not measure keyboard navigation, compositor rendering, or that the frontend launches under its real desktop — those stay the VM walkthrough's job.
